variants.name: Composable callables (lambdas / std::function)
variants.implementation_notes: Modern C++ replaces the specification class hierarchy with a single function type: a rule is any callable satisfying std::predicate - a lambda held in std::function<bool(const T&)> when it must be stored, or a template parameter when it need not be - and composition is either a combined lambda body (`[&](const Invoice& i){ return overdue(i) && !in_collection(i); }`) or a small combinator returning a new closure. Algorithms consume the predicate directly through std::ranges::filter_view, remove_if or a plain loop. A named class with virtual operator() remains justified when rules are registered from configuration, serialized, or translated into a query, or when evaluation through std::function is too costly: prefer a template parameter or a plain lambda on hot paths because std::function type-erases and may allocate.
pitfalls: Capturing by reference in a rule stored beyond the current scope leaves dangling references; store owning copies for rules that outlive their factory.
std::function erases the type and may allocate; on hot paths keep the callable as a template parameter or use std::function_ref-style non-owning wrappers.
An empty std::function throws std::bad_function_call when invoked - a default-constructed or moved-from rule must be avoided or checked.

variants.name: Abstract Specification hierarchy with And/Or/Not subclasses
variants.implementation_notes: The pattern text's original C++ form: an abstract template base declaring `virtual bool operator()(const T&) const = 0;`, one leaf subclass per rule, and And/Or/Not composites holding children in a std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Specification<T>>>. Choose it when rules are instantiated from configuration or a registry at runtime, must be named in logs, or must be dynamically combined from data, and when the toolchain is pre-C++11; otherwise the callable form is less code and avoids a virtual call per candidate and per child.
pitfalls: Storing children by value slices them; composites must hold pointers/references with an explicit ownership policy (unique_ptr, or non-owning raw pointers with a documented lifetime).
Deep rule trees pay a virtual call per node per candidate; hoist invariant checks and keep the tree shallow on hot paths.
The base destructor must be virtual, otherwise deleting through Specification<T>* is undefined behaviour.
